chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn Aʿyan, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A woman died and left behind her husband, her maternal brothers, and her paternal brothers. He said:

The husband has one-half, which is three shares. The maternal brothers have one-third, in which the male and the female are equal. One share remains, and it belongs to the paternal brothers and sisters.
For the male is the like of the share of two females.

key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ ٱلْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: the male receives the share of two females
key_terms.ٱلزَّوْجِ: the husband as an inheriting spouse
key_terms.ٱلْإِخْوَةِ لِلْأُمِّ: maternal siblings who inherit equally here
key_terms.ٱلْإِخْوَةِ وَ ٱلْأَخَوَاتِ مِنَ ٱلْأَبِ: paternal siblings who receive the remainder

ai.seo_question: How is a woman’s inheritance divided between her husband, maternal siblings, and paternal siblings in Shia law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the inheritance of a deceased woman who leaves behind a husband, maternal siblings, and paternal siblings. It specifies the fixed shares: one-half for the husband, one-third for the maternal siblings equally between male and female, and the remainder for the paternal siblings with the male receiving the share of two females. The report is significant in Shia fiqh for clarifying the distribution of inheritance among different classes of siblings.
